title: FARDC-Wazalendo Confirm Kasake Recapture, Push Into Kalehe's Nteko-Miko M23 Command Post
detail: FARDC and allied Wazalendo fighters confirmed the recapture of Kasake in Masisi's Bahunde chiefdom on Thursday, Sept 17, a day after fighting first broke out there, consolidating a week-long counteroffensive that had already retaken Miko hill, Katuunda, Remeka and Kaleta in Masisi and Mindjendje in Walikale. The push extended south into South Kivu's Kalehe territory, where government-aligned forces recaptured the villages of Mutara, Kivoka, Tushungute and Kashovu along with AFC/M23's Nteko-Miko command post — a first reversal of M23's Kalehe gains since the rebels overran the Ziralo grouping in mid-August. Military sources said one M23 commander and ten fighters were captured during the operations. No comprehensive casualty toll was available, and AFC/M23 did not publicly confirm the losses.

title: Clashes Flare at Burora Hill Near Ngungu in Masisi's Ufamandu I Grouping
detail: Heavy and light weapons fire rang out through the night of Sept 16-17 around Burora hill, near Ngungu in Masisi's Ufamandu I grouping, as AFC/M23 rebels clashed with FARDC and allied Wazalendo fighters. Actualite.cd sources described intensifying combat overnight; no casualty figures were available. A separate Actualite.cd front-line survey published Sept 18 listed the wider Ngungu area among positions held by FARDC and Wazalendo, suggesting government forces retained the area after this clash.

media.caption: Masisi territory, North Kivu, where clashes were reported around Burora hill near Ngungu, Sept 16-17, 2026

confidenceReason: Reported by a single outlet (Actualite.cd) citing its own local sources; no FARDC or AFC/M23 official statement, though a same-outlet Sept 18 survey lists Ngungu as FARDC/Wazalendo-held, offering partial corroboration.

title: Ebola Toll Reaches 3,577 Deaths Among 7,404 Cases as Ituri Transmission May Be Peaking
detail: DRC's Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak reached 7,404 confirmed cases and 3,577 deaths as of Sept 15 data — a case-fatality rate of 48.3%, with 1,776 patients recovered — across 62 health zones in 7 provinces. Ituri remains the epicenter with 77.7% of cases, though National Institute of Biomedical Research director Jean-Jacques Muyembe said the province's transmission curve 'has reached a peak and is beginning to decrease.' North Kivu's weekly case count nearly doubled over two weeks, from roughly 100 to more than 200, with isolation-bed occupancy at 94.7%. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the epidemic 'continues to progress and continues to claim lives,' while epidemic-response director Maria Van Kerkhove said the response remains 'far from finished.'

title: Triple Killing of Money Changer, Wife and Moto-Taxi Driver Prompts Security Demands in Beni
detail: Unidentified armed attackers killed a money changer, his wife and a motorcycle-taxi driver in the Butanuka neighborhood of Beni's Beu commune during the week of Sept 9-16; no suspects had been identified as of Radio Okapi's Sept 17 report. The city's money-changers' corporation demanded intensified security patrols and the involvement of intelligence and police services to identify perpetrators, citing a pattern of armed robberies targeting cash-handling currency traders. Beni Mayor Jacob Nyofondo Te Kodale said security services were mobilized to pursue the killers and restore order.

title: FARDC Communiqué Claims 14 AFC/M23 Fighters Killed Across Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru
detail: A FARDC military communiqué issued Thursday, Sept 17, 2026 by spokesperson Major Dieudonné Kasereka said combined FARDC-Wazalendo forces killed 14 AFC/M23 combatants, wounded 13 and captured 3 in fighting across Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru territories between Sept 15-17, while recovering the strategic Miko and Remeka hills and the Kasheke village center. The army said 3 Wazalendo (VDP) fighters were killed and 8 weapons were seized from rebel positions. Kasereka said FARDC forces "will defend ourselves, because we must respond appropriately to all these provocations." AFC/M23 did not publicly confirm the toll.
